thesis: He doesn't shield you, he takes it. Exhaustion and a little contempt, not devotion. He'd rather eat the hit than trust you to avoid it.

posture._comment: APPLIED AFTER RIGGING, never baked into the T-pose mesh. Mixamo's auto-rigger requires left/right symmetry; a lopsided T-pose confuses marker placement and skinning. These are bone offsets the renderer applies on top of every Mixamo clip, so the hunch survives idle, walk, dash and death alike. See docs/ART_PIPELINE.md §3.

magic._comment: Never warm. A paladin's light is given to him; Aegis forces his. Pale, sickly, effortful.

mainHand._comment: A salvaged bulkhead, not a heater or a tower. Too heavy. Dragged, not carried.

attach._comment: Where the door rides: on the OUTER SURFACE of the right forearm, centred along it (owner's calls, 2026-08-22). The forearm rather than the hand because a salvaged bulkhead is strapped to the arm, and that arm is never free — a hand grip would let him put it down. Offsets are in the bone's local space, position in TILES, rotation in XYZ degrees. y=0.11 is the forearm's midpoint (the bone is 0.227 tiles long), so the door is centred on the limb. z=-0.10 lifts it clear: the door's face normal is bone -Z after the rotation below, so a negative z sets its BACK against the arm instead of running the arm through its middle — at z=0 the pauldron poked straight through the panel. Rotation: -90 about Z takes the door off the arm's axis (a bone's local +Y runs down the bone), and 180 about Y turns its face — and the 47 tally marks — outward rather than into his chest.

vfxLanguage._comment: He has exactly one idea and he keeps having it. Every effect is a slab of the same cold light, the same proportion as the door on his arm.

style._comment: blockiness is the superellipse exponent: 2 = round, 4 = squircle, 8+ = boxy. The single knob that moves the whole roster between silhouette languages.

_weaponClassNote: A salvaged bulkhead strapped to one arm. That arm is never free.

clips._comment: Clip names as they appear in build/.../aegis.glb, from the Mixamo downloads. Per character by nature — Aegis's attack is aegis_smash, not a generic 'attack'. The ability mapping is a Designer call; this one is the owner's (2026-08-21): warding_halo is the ultimate and takes aegis_ultimate, and barrier_pulse shares warding_wall_cast with warding_wall. Two abilities sharing a clip is fine — the client looks clips up by name.
